ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.36 (excess distance fare for the 2.38 km of the 21:43–21:50 detour not covered by the rider's general route instruction) to the original payment method; log the RD-4 roadworks finding and issue the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder on his route compliance record, and record a driver violation (no traffic reason for the portion driven, RD-4) — no flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 14.9 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, a 4.2 km deviation [F1], far above the 1 km tolerance in RD-1, and the single off-route segment 21:43–21:50 drove 5.14 km where the optimal route covers 1.44 km, adding 3.70 km via Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road [F3]. So RD-1 is met and RD-2's refund matrix applies unless the segment is exempt.

The rider's only pre-segment words were sent at 21:38: "Whatever road you think is fastest, I trust you, don't need to follow the app" [F7], accepted by the driver at 21:38 [F8], in a complete, fully timestamped two-message chat [F9]. That is a general route choice, not a named road; it covers a route chosen to get from Orchard Road to NUS, and it was given before the segment began, so the timing rule in RD-5 is satisfied. RD-3 is not in play: no stop was requested or measured in the segment [F3].

But the general route choice does not cover everything the driver did. His own account is that he "thought Telok Blangah Road would be faster at that hour" [F10] — a driver's post-hoc statement is not consent, but it is an admission of his own route choice. Under RD-5 a general route choice covers a route chosen to get there, not a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing. Reading the road name as written, "JALAN BUKIT MERAH" is Jalan Bukit Merah, the road through Bukit Merah, which lies astride the direct corridor from Orchard Road to NUS; the rider left that choice to the driver, so the portion of the segment within that corridor is exempt (named_road_tied; it is not a named_road_elsewhere case, because the rider named no road at all and F3 lists the roads driven, so code can tie the agreement to the corridor). The detour through Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road is off that corridor; the driver admits he took it on his own judgement [F10] under a general instruction, which is the errand branch of RD-5 ("a loop that reaches nothing still counts"). That part of the segment counts.

4.18 km × ($1.32/5.14 km = $0.2568/km) = $1.07 for the 4.18 km of detour in that window [F3]; less the exempt Jalan Bukit Merah portion, 5.14 km × (1.44/5.14) = 1.44 km → a further 1.44 km × $0.2568/km = $0.37 exempt (the stated 1.44 km optimal-corridor kilometres, RD-5); $1.07 − $0.37 = $0.70; plus the 3.70 km outside the window at the trip's billed rate, 3.70 km × $0.7201/km = $2.66 [F3, F4]; $0.70 + $2.66 = $3.36 [RD-2].

No traffic reason exempts the segment: the AYE ran at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and the CTE at band 8 during the trip window, no incident was recorded near the route, weather was fair [F11][F12][F13][F14], and the trace's screen returns no qualifying incident or congestion for the replaced stretch — so RD-4 never exempts, and RD-2 requires a driver violation to be recorded and RD-7 a notification-duty reminder to the driver. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route deviations in 90 days [F16], and his profile otherwise decides nothing.
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; undetermined reading of RD-5:scope

segment_findings.reason: Rider's pre-segment message [F7] ('Whatever road you think is fastest, I trust you') is a general route choice under RD-5, accepted at 21:38 [F8], which covers a route chosen to reach NUS but not a separate off-corridor loop (Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road, Henderson Road) that RD-5 says counts; yet the segment also traverses Jalan Bukit Merah, on the direct Orchard Road–NUS corridor — the expressway route runs at 60–69 km/h [F11] but the CTE, the direct corridor, also ran at 70+ km/h [F12], so the exempt portion cannot be measured from the record. RD-5 and RD-2 leave the share exempt undetermined, which changes the amount, so a person must settle it.

element_findings.reason: The rider's words are a general route choice [F7], consented before the segment [F8], so RD-5 general_route_consent applies; but scope cannot be read on this record: the segment's roads [F3] include both Jalan Bukit Merah on the direct Orchard Road–NUS corridor (where the driver's choice [F10] was authorised, and the CTE there ran at 70+ km/h [F12]) and the off-corridor loop through Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road, which no rider message asked for and which RD-5 says counts. How much of the 5.14 km segment is exempt cannot be read from the words, so the share is undetermined.

rejected_claims.reason: The 4.2 km deviation and 1 km tolerance are right [F1][RD-1], but the claim that all excess distance is refundable fails in part: RD-5 exempts the portion covered by the rider's pre-trip general route instruction [F7][F8].

The segment measurements are correct [F3][RD-1], but the claim frames the whole 3.70 km as refundable; the rider's general route choice [F7] covers the Jalan Bukit Merah corridor kilometres, and the exempt share is undetermined on this record [RD-5].

Accepted as to RD-4: no traffic reason exists on the record [F11][F12][F13][F14], so a driver violation is recorded and the RD-7 reminder applies; but no traffic reason never exempts a segment — the refund turns only on the rider's agreement [RD-2][RD-4][RD-5].

The $5.89 figure is the 4.18 km × $1.4098/km billed excess [F4][F6], but the refund is computed per RD-2 by leaving out exempt kilometres, and the refund rate is the trip's own metres' rate ÷ distance, not the 4.18 km billed rate [RD-2].

The reading of F7 as general route consent is adopted [F7][F8][RD-5], but it does not follow that no kilometre is covered: under RD-5 a general route choice covers the route chosen to get there, including the Jalan Bukit Merah corridor the driver took, while only the off-corridor loop counts.

RD-5 notice timing is not decisive here: the rider's own 21:38 message [F7] supplied the prior agreement, so no further notice was required for the corridor portion, and F10 [F10] is the driver's claim on scope, not on timing [RD-5].
Duration 18.8 min vs 17.3 min is a recorded +1.5 min [F2], but time fare and discomfort are not refundable items under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

Correct that RD-2's violation and RD-7's reminder follow from the absent traffic reason [F13][RD-4], and correct that RD-6 is not triggered [F16][RD-6]; but these are consequences of the ruling, not an exemption for the driver.
The rider's clean profile [F15] is recorded, but profile facts never decide a case alone [RD-5].
Accepted that F7 is a general route choice given before the trip [F7][F8][RD-5], but a general choice does not exempt an off-corridor loop of the driver's own choosing under RD-5.
Timing is agreed [F3][F7], but RD-5 consent must also cover the segment; the record does not settle that the general choice covered the whole 5.14 km detour [RD-5].
The rider named no road [F7][F3], so the agreement cannot be tied to the roads driven: the named-road check fails for the corridor route and the exempt share is undetermined [RD-5].
RD-4 does not exempt any segment; the absence of traffic cause fixes the refund and the violation, and the rider's consent is general, not a route to the off-corridor loop [F11][F13][F7][RD-4][RD-5].
Accepted that F10 shows no errand stop [F10][F3], but RD-4 requires traffic data for the replaced stretch at trip time, which F11 and F13 contradict [RD-4].
The distances and the $5.89 billed excess are agreed [F1][F3][F4], but the request that no excess kilometre be refunded is refused: the off-corridor portion counts under RD-2.

Tolls, time fare, the platform fee and the 1.0× surge are not refunded [F4][F5][F6][RD-2], but the ask that the fare be upheld in full fails because the deviation exceeds the 1 km tolerance [F1][RD-1].
The driver's record shows 0 upheld route deviations in 90 days [F16], so no RD-6 flag is applied; the record is otherwise not a defence to the deviation [RD-6].
